subject: Performance SLO: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted vs current provider)  FinLytics
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@finlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Performance SLO: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted vs current provider) - FinLytics

Hi Samir -

Thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps: 

What we heard from FinLytics:
- Primary use: real-time customer-facing summarization and risk-scoring flows tied to trading alerts.
- Production traffic target: ~200 RPS peak, sustained 60-80 RPS.
- Concurrency target: ~50 concurrent sessions for the summary flow.
- Typical prompt size: ~120 tokens; average generated response: ~400-500 tokens.
- Streaming: yes - client streams tokens as they arrive for the summary flow.
- Current provider metrics: you mentioned higher tail latency and occasional spikes impacting UX.

Open items we asked for on the call:
1) Precise end-to-end p95/p99 numbers you see today (including network + client-to-provider time).
2) Whether the streaming endpoint is the critical path for UX (vs batch).
3) A short traffic sample (1-2k request traces or a CSV with timestamps, request size, and observed latency) so we can baseline.

Attached is our Redwood SLO playbook (redwood_slo_playbook.pdf) with example acceptance criteria and how we measure end-to-end p95/p99 across hosted vs dedicated deployments.

Proposed next steps:
- You send the latency sample and any recent p95/p99 numbers.
- Aditya and I run a lightweight benchmark and propose a target SLO and rollout plan (hosted API quickproof, then Dedicated if you want reserved capacity).
- 30-min technical sync this week to align on tracing identifiers and an initial test window.

Would Wednesday 7/22 10:00am PT work for a short sync? If not, send a couple of time options.

Thanks - looking forward to getting you a clear baseline and a proposal.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
[attachment: redwood_slo_playbook.pdf]

From: Samir Shah <samir@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted vs current provider) - FinLytics

Marissa -

Thanks for the recap and the playbook. Quick answers while I pull the CSV you requested (should send in an hour):

Current provider numbers (end-to-end, client -> provider -> client) for our summary flow over last 7 days:
- Non-streaming (single response): p95 = 2,200 ms, p99 = 4,200 ms
- Streaming (token-by-token): p95 = 1,800 ms, p99 = 3,500 ms

Traffic/size details:
- Peak: ~210 RPS (spiky during market opens)
- Sustained: 60-85 RPS
- Concurrency: observed up to 55 concurrent summary sessions during spikes
- Prompt tokens: median 120, 95th percentile 240
- Response tokens: median 420, 95th percentile 900

Key UX impact: the p99 spikes on streaming are the main problem - some clients see >6s perceived latency when the tail blows up. We currently do a simple retry which sometimes just makes the tail worse.

I'll attach our raw export in a minute (finlytics_current_latency.csv). Also happy to jump on Wed 7/22 10am PT.

-Samir
Head of Engineering | FinLytics
samir@finlytics.com
[attachment: finlytics_current_latency.csv]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-07-20T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted vs current provider) - FinLytics

Samir -

Perfect, that's extremely helpful. A couple of clarifying notes and a suggested acceptance criteria for a hosted proof-of-value:

Clarifying Qs (so we can set the right test harness):
- Are the numbers you shared measured from your client (browser/mobile) or from your backend service? We want to know if CDN/edge network time is included.
- When you say streaming p99 = 3.5s, is that time-to-first-byte for the generated stream or time-to-final-token?
- Any hard SLA requirement for tail latency we should be aware of (e.g., "must not exceed 2s for 99% of requests")?

Suggested hosted PV acceptance criteria (initial goal):
- End-to-end p95 <= 800 ms and p99 <= 2,000 ms for the streaming summary flow under a 60-80 RPS sustained load and 50 concurrent sessions (we can tune based on your real traces).
- For burst/peak windows up to 200 RPS, graceful degradation with a prioritized routing policy and measurable error budget.

We find the best approach is: you share the CSV traces, we replay a scaled 1-1 reproduction in our test harness (ingesting the same token sizes and inter-arrival distribution), and then run 3 controlled runs against hosted API + your preferred model. If we hit acceptance criteria, we produce a short report and a recommended Dedicated configuration if you want an SLA-backed rollout.

I've attached a 1-page mutual action plan that outlines roles and timing (mutual_action_plan_finlytics.pdf).

If Wed 7/22 10am PT works, Aditya and I will use that time to confirm tracing keys and the sample pull method.

Thanks -
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
[attachment: mutual_action_plan_finlytics.pdf]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@finlytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-21T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted vs current provider) - FinLytics

Hi Samir -

Thanks for sharing the trace export. A few quick technical follow-ups so we can design an apples-to-apples benchmark: 

1) Please confirm whether your traces include DNS + TLS handshake time (client -> internet) or are measured from your backend service after connection reuse. If you can, mark a sample trace ID and I'll correlate.

2) For streaming: is your client expecting chunked transfer with first-token latency visibility? Our streaming measurement will report: time-to-first-token and time-to-final-token. Which one matters for UX?

3) Tokenization details: do you use approximate token counts from your app, or can you provide raw text for 10 representative requests so we can run the same tokenizer?

Planned benchmark (what we'll run during the sync):
- Replay of 2k requests scaled to your 60-80 RPS sustained profile and a peak window to 200 RPS.
- 50 concurrent session simulation, streaming enabled.
- Run 3 iterations against the hosted API (same model you currently use; we can also test our recommended quantized variant).
- Collect end-to-end p95/p99, time-to-first-token (streaming), and CPU/GPU utilization on our side.

If that sounds good I'll create a short runbook and share the test endpoints and minimal curl examples ahead of the meeting. Looking forward to the sync on 7/22 10am PT.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
